title: After the Attacker Leaves: Benchmarking Carryover Attacks on LLM Agents

object.carrier: Persistent workspace files the runtime reads back: memory/MEMORY.md silently prepended to the system prompt at every new session, and HEARTBEAT.md scheduled tasks fired by the heartbeat daemon (default 30-min interval; Hermes cron jobs.json on 60s tick). A one-time indirect prompt injection (email/webpage/document/tool return) is planted via the agent's own write_file and re-fires in later sessions after the attacker exits with zero persistent presence.

safety_property.statement: A one-time indirect prompt injection committed to long-term memory or a scheduled task must not re-fire as harmful action (exfiltrating payroll/financial/medical content to attacker URLs, rerouting payments, unauthorized sends) in later sessions after the attacker leaves; in the evaluated agents the planted payload persists across sessions and, conditional on successful planting, is executed almost deterministically, so trigger-time protection largely fails while confidentiality (exfiltration), integrity (payment rerouting) and policy-compliance (unauthorized autonomous actions) are all violated.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Deterministic rule-based verifier matches attacker markers (URL/recipient/path) in tool-call role fields over N=5 independent follow-up sessions; attack success decomposed as ASR = Pr(Plant) x Pr(Trig|Plant) with per-round N-TrigRate, reported jointly with gated benign-task Utility.

capabilities: One-time indirect prompt injection into resources the agent reads: webpages, emails, documents, or tool return values
Persuades the agent to commit the payload to MEMORY.md or HEARTBEAT.md via the agent's own write_file
Exits after the single injection with zero persistent presence; later firings require no further attacker action
assumptions: The runtime persists state across sessions via long-lived memory files silently prepended to the system prompt and heartbeat/cron scheduled tasks
The agent can edit its own persistent files (write_file), so anything written becomes a standing instruction
The attacker cannot modify the runtime, cannot read/write MEMORY.md or HEARTBEAT.md directly, and cannot bypass OS access control
not_covered: Always-on adversaries that remain present across sessions (AgentLAB-style)
Direct write access to MEMORY.md/HEARTBEAT.md or runtime modification
Adaptive/multi-step attackers that react to defenses at trigger time
Reasoning-mode Gemini-3.1-Pro in the Hermes runtime ablation (excluded due to variable per-call latency)
Real multi-day session diversity for Latent triggering (identical domain-natural follow-ups replayed instead)

intervention.name: D1 (system-prompt principles), D2 (explicit edit authority), D3 (harness-level provenance marking / Spotlighting envelope)
intervention.description: D1 prepends a generic safety-principles block via AGENTS.md (authority provenance, task-scope adherence, persistent-state caution, egress proportionality); D2 grants the agent explicit authority to inspect, edit and remove MEMORY.md/HEARTBEAT.md entries; D3 wraps persistent-state reads in an <untrusted_persistent_state trust="low"> envelope at the context-injection layer (delimiting variant of Spotlighting). The paper's shared-ceiling analysis: all three reach the model only as text alongside the planted instruction, so they concentrate at the plant stage and leave the trigger gate largely unresolved; closing the trigger gate is argued to require out-of-channel runtime controls (capability sandboxing, outbound-egress allowlists, persistent-state write quarantine), consistent with the Hermes runtime ablation.

controls.name: Shared system prompt, tool-call template and temperature 0 across the five models
D.2 follow-up conditions (Replay / Paraphrase / Same-domain different-intent / Unrelated) for Latent triggering

results.claim: Harness-level provenance marking (D3 spotlighting envelope) reduces Qwen3-235B-A22B overall carryover ASR from 66.7% to 48.5% almost entirely by suppressing planting (plant 78.8% -> 56.1%), while the conditional trigger gate is untouched (T|P-Auto 89.3% -> 90.0%).

limitations.statement: The rule-based verifier has finite marker aliases, so false negatives dominate; reported ASR should be read as a relative signal across models, not a point estimate of true vulnerability.
limitations.quote: The ASR values we report should be read as a relative signal across models rather than a point estimate of true vulnerability.

limitations.statement: Latent trigger rounds replay an identical domain-natural follow-up, so the reported P(trig|plant) for Latent is an upper bound on realistic trigger rates, measuring planting persuasion under topical alignment rather than cumulative deployment harm.
limitations.quote: The reported P⁡(trig∣plant)P(\mathrm{trig}\mid\mathrm{plant}) for Latent should therefore be read as an upper bound on realistic trigger rates—it measures planting persuasion under topical alignment, not cumulative deployment harm under realistic session distributions.

limitations.statement: The Hermes runtime ablation covers only non-reasoning configurations, excluding Gemini-3.1-Pro due to highly variable per-call latency; reasoning effects are probed separately only on Qwen3-235B-A22B.
limitations.quote: excluding Gemini-3.1-Pro due to highly variable per-call latency under reasoning in Hermes pilot runs. We separately examine the effect of enabling reasoning on Qwen3-235B-A22B in Appendix D.4.

limitations.statement: The schema-framing ablation runs on a single task family (travel_booking), and its only cross-model pattern (F-class advantage in autonomous mode on highly-defended models) rests on directional evidence from two models.
limitations.quote: The supporting evidence is therefore directional voting from two models—we report it as a tentative observation rather than a robust finding.

limitations.statement: The single model-channel cell where D3 closed the trigger gate (GLM-5 Autonomous) is a one-trial effect within rerun noise.
limitations.quote: a same-day no-D3 rerun shows a comparable Pr⁡(trig∣plant)\Pr(\text{trig}\mid\text{plant}) deviation, placing the effect within rerun noise.
